title: Indostar Capital Finance Ltd - 541336 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IndoStar Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR13 crore on a INR49 crore overlay release; disbursements up 51% YoY to INR1,399 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 disbursements reached INR1,399 crore, up 51% YoY and 13% QoQ, with vehicle finance at INR1,325 crore and Micro LAP at INR74 crore. Net total income was INR242 crore versus INR190 crore a year earlier, and PAT was INR13 crore versus INR11 crore. Reported profit was helped by the release of a INR49 crore precautionary overlay created in Q4 FY26, while the credit cost was INR96 crore. Gross Stage 3 fell to 4.5% from 4.8%, and management said legacy pre-January 2025 book is running down toward about 10% of AUM by end-FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +51% YoY; vs INR1,235 crore in Q1 FY27
Retail 97% of AUM; retail AUM INR8,204 crore
vs INR81 crore in previous quarter; after INR49 crore overlay release

segments.name: Vehicle finance
segments.commentary: Q2 disbursements INR1,325 crore, up 47% YoY; AUM INR7,923 crore. Passenger vehicle disbursements up about 75% over last year; MHCV share of disbursements fell from 31% to 27% and PV rose from 23% to 31%.

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: Q2 disbursements INR74 crore (+174% YoY); AUM INR280 crore (+177% YoY); 99.6% current, 90+ DPD 0.18%, weighted average LTV below 40%, average ticket size INR8.9 lakh vs INR6 lakh a year ago.

guidance_outlook: Normalised credit cost guided at 2% to 2.5%; management expects a much smaller credit cost in FY28 than FY27, with reduction visible from Q4 FY27.
Pre-January 2025 book expected to fall to about 10% of AUM by end of FY27; provisioning expected to fall significantly from Q4 FY27.
Target of 35% CAGR in disbursements over 3 years and PAT of INR450-500 crore in FY29, both reiterated.
ROAA target of 2% from H2 FY28 as legacy book runs off; current ROAA stated at about 0.5%.
Micro LAP target of 10-15% of the book in 3 years; LAP launch planned in Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh over Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Branch network to add about 100 branches over 3 years; 454 to 475 branches in last two quarters.
Management expects to pass on the repo-rate hike to borrowers, as most peers plan to do.
capex_capacity: Branches at 475 (up from 454 two quarters ago); guidance of about 100 additions over 3 years, equal to 7-10% network growth.
Co-located LAP operations now in 154 branches across 9 states and 1 union territory, after Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal went live in Aug-Sep 2026; 71 branches in 2 states a year earlier.
Field sales force raised from about 1,235 to 1,868 over the last year (+51%); about 400-strong dedicated hot-bucket collection team added.
STP rate of 74% in used car and 68% in CV via bureau scorecards.
Data science practice set up in Feb 2026; next two quarters to roll out self-service BI layer, settlement model and acquisition scorecards for new car, MLAP, farm and construction equipment.
demand_pricing: Industry: NBFC vehicle finance credit grew 15.4% YoY as of Aug 2026; non-food bank credit grew 19.4% by Sept 2026.
Customer quality: share of prime customers (CIBIL 725+) in portfolio rose to 85% from 80% a year ago and 62% in Q2 FY24; borrowers with CIBIL 700+ at 95% of last quarter's disbursements.
30+ DPD on disbursements from Jan to Sep 2026 is 71% lower than for Jan to Sep 2024 disbursements.
Early delinquency stable at about 2.4%; non-starter ratio 1.7%; new-to-credit share cut to about 4% from 14%.
Micro LAP disbursement yield about 20% plus upfront fees; alternate channels (connectors and DSAs) contribute 20-25%.
Effective yield on P&L (revenue from operations) 15.5% vs 15.1% in Q1; NIM 8.9% including DA income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did loan yields rise from 16.5% to 17.6% while NIM rose only 10 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 17.6% is origination yield including DA assignment income; on the P&L, revenue from operations yield rose from 15.1% to 15.5%, and NIM of 8.9% includes DA income.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the M&HCV share of the vehicle book settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will avoid concentration above 35-40% in any single segment across its five verticals (MLAP, CV, FE, PV, CE).

qa_highlights.question: When will provisioning come down significantly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pre-Jan 2025 book (about INR1,850 crore, 24% of AUM, 27% of it 30+ DPD) drives provisions of about INR96-100 crore per quarter; provisions should fall significantly from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is AUM growth (about 12% YoY) well below disbursement growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the INR132 crore direct assignment and write-offs of high-delinquency legacy assets; the gap is expected to narrow as the old book runs off.

qa_highlights.question: Why release the INR49 crore overlay in a tricky macro?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stress had not materialised, monthly portfolio performance kept improving, and the recalibrated ECL model covers actual losses.

qa_highlights.question: How is the borrowing cost likely to move with the repo hike?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR3,900 crore of borrowings are floating or due within a year; about INR1,000 crore is linked to repo, T-bill or MCLR and may reprice higher, while about INR1,300 crore at over 10.5% will reprice lower. Overall cost expected to fall.

risks_watch: Legacy pre-Jan 2025 book still at about 24% of AUM, with 27% of it 30+ DPD, so forward flows could still hit provisions.
Repo-rate hike (25 bps to 5.50%) to reprice about INR1,000 crore of floating borrowings; passing it on to borrowers depends on peers and competition.
Overlay released in Q2 after the West Asia and fuel-price concern; reported PAT depends on credit cost falling as guided.
Gap between disbursement growth (about 50%) and AUM growth (about 12%) must narrow for the 18-20% AUM growth view.
Micro LAP is unseasoned; expansion to Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh in Q3-Q4 FY27 is untested.
Recoveries from the corporate and retail stressed-asset portfolios (ARC sales) expected over 12-24 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on asset quality trends, customer mix and the run-off of the legacy book, with growth targets reiterated. Evasive or unclear when pressed on yield and NIM bridges, and it needed follow-up on the origination versus P&L yield figures.
key_quotes: But the good news is by end of this year, the overall book goes down to around 10% of the AUM.
We do want to target 2% ROAA from H2 FY28 because by that time, most of our old book would have run off.

With the stress not materializing and our recalibrated ECL model adequately covering actual losses, we have released the overlay of INR49 crores in Q2 FY27, while continuing to monitor the situation closely.
we would expect our normalized credit cost to remain between 2% to 2.5%.

adds.what: About 100 new branches over 3 years (network at 475, up from 454 two quarters ago)
LAP launch in Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh

growth.why: Management reiterates 35% disbursement CAGR and INR450-500 crore FY29 PAT, backed by a 51% YoY disbursement rise to INR1,399 crore, 154 co-located LAP branches and ~100 planned branch additions over 3 years, but no capex or order figures are given and the PAT figure is flattered by a INR49 crore overlay release.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Pre-Jan 2025 book (about 24% of AUM, provisions about INR96-100 crore a quarter) is guided to fall significantly from Q4 FY27, and ROAA is targeted at 2% from H2 FY28 versus about 0.5% now; cost of borrowing already fell to 9.7% (incremental 9.1%), though about INR1,000 crore of floating debt may reprice higher after the 25 bps repo hike.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branches rose from 454 to 475 in two quarters and management guides about 100 additions over 3 years (7-10% network growth), with LAP launches in Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh slated for Q3 and Q4 FY27 and the co-located LAP network at 154 branches.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Disbursements rose 51% YoY to INR1,399 crore (H1 FY27 INR2,634 crore) with the 35% three-year disbursement CAGR reiterated, but AUM growth is only about 12% YoY, so the gap must narrow for the 18-20% AUM view.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation are not discussed; the branch rollout is opex-led and no plant or capacity capex figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated the INR450-500 crore FY29 PAT target and expects credit cost to fall from FY27 to FY28, but the Q2 PAT of INR13 crore was flattered by a INR49 crore overlay release, so an upgrade is not yet supported by underlying earnings.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost was INR96 crore in Q2 (INR81 crore in Q1) before the overlay release, provisions depend on the legacy book running down as guided, and the 2-2.5% normalised credit cost is new guidance that could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: LAP launch planned in Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh over Q3 and Q4 FY27 with a 10-15% of book target in 3 years (Micro LAP AUM INR280 crore, +177% YoY).

rows.label: Legacy book run-off to about 10% of AUM by FY27 end
rows.why: Pre-Jan 2025 book is about 24% of AUM (about INR1,850 crore) and management expects it to fall to about 10% by end FY27, which would release provisioning pressure.

rows.label: Borrowing cost reset and repricing
rows.why: Weighted average borrowing cost fell to 9.7% with incremental cost at 9.1%, and about INR1,300 crore above 10.5% will reprice lower, against about INR1,000 crore of floating debt that may reprice higher after the repo hike.

rows.label: Pass-through of repo hike to borrowers
rows.why: Management expects to pass the 25 bps repo hike to borrowers as most peers plan to, but this depends on peers and competition.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality, customer mix, legacy run-off and reiterated FY29 targets, but was evasive on the origination versus P&L yield and NIM bridge, and analysts had to follow up on those numbers.
